metadata.title: Guideline on Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (Food and Drugs Authority, Ghana)
metadata.edition: FDA/SMD/GDL-03/07, Version 07, in effect 29 January 2025 · 3.1 QPPV resident in Ghana; 3.1.1(d) vacancy notified within 14 days
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Ghana guideline under the Public Health Act 2012 (Act 851); the Act prevails.
metadata.applicability: Applicants, sponsors and market authorization holders reporting ICSRs (see the PV Info ICSR rulebook for scope).

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.statement: Executive summary Marketing Authorization Holders/Manufacturers (MAHs) whose products have been granted marketing authorization in Ghana have a responsibility of establishing a pharmacovigilance system in fulfilment of the Public Health, 2012, Act 851 Part 7, Section 125, subsection 1. To this end, MAHs are required to appoint a Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) to ensure the establishment and maintenance of a pharmacovigilance system.
candidates.context: 5.0 Penalities ................................................................................................................ 14 APPENDIX I: TEMPLATE CONTRACT FOR QPPV ..................................................... 15 APPENDIX II: APPLICATION FORM FOR RE-DESIGNATION AS A QPPV .............. 17 APPENDIX III: QPPV DECLARATION FOR RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN ................ 19 The guidelines for qualified person for pharmacovigilance is published for the information, guidance and strict compliance by MAHs/Manufacturers to ensure the safe and rational use of medical products, thereby improving patient safety and public health.

candidates.statement: The key responsibilities of the MAH which include the provision of comprehensive training in pharmacovigilance (PV) to the QPPV and ensure that the QPPV has sufficient authority to implement PV activities are defined in the guidelines. The required information that needs to be submitted to the Authority relating to the QPPV is outlined in this guideline.
candidates.context: The guidelines for qualified person for pharmacovigilance is published for the information, guidance and strict compliance by MAHs/Manufacturers to ensure the safe and rational use of medical products, thereby improving patient safety and public health. The guideline outlines the responsibilities of the QPPV and the requirements for re-designation following a three-year expiration period. The sanctions and penalties that will be applied in case of non-compliance to the requirements in the guidelines by the Local Representative, MAH/Manufacturer are detailed in these guidelines.

candidates.statement: 3.1 General Requirements The Marketing Authorization Holder shall permanently and continuously have at his disposal an appropriately Qualified Person Responsible for Pharmacovigilance. The Qualified Person Responsible for Pharmacovigilance shall be resident in Ghana.

candidates.statement: 3.2 Information to be submitted to the Authority by the MAH The MAH shall submit the following information to the Authority relating to the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance a. curriculum vitae including key information on the role of the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance b. contact details including but not limited to the name, telephone, fax and e-mail, postal and official working address c. a description of the responsibilities guaranteeing that the QPPV has sufficient authority over the pharmacovigilance system in order to promote, maintain and improve compliance;
candidates.context: e. Have written a contract with the QPPV d. details of back-up arrangements to apply in the absence of the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance; and e. a list of tasks that have been delegated by the qualified person for pharmacovigilance and to whom these tasks have been delegated.

candidates.statement: 3.3.1 Qualifications of QPPV i. The person designated as Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) shall be healthcare professional with BSc Medicine, B.
candidates.context: 3.3 Specific Requirements Pharmacy, BSc Nursing, BSc Physician Assistantship or any other healthcare professional degree recognized by the Authority.

candidates.statement: iii. The QPPV shall receive a formal training in pharmacovigilance
candidates.context: ii. The Authority may also accept a person with a relevant scientific discipline with at least two years minimum experience with specific job function in the area of pharmacovigilance for designation as the QPPV. recognized by the Authority.

candidates.statement: 3.3.2 Back-up QPPV i. With the exception of section 3.3.1 subsection iii , the Back-up QPPV shall meet all the requirements of a QPPV. The Back-up QPPV shall however receive training in pharmacovigilance appropriate for his/her roles.
candidates.context: recognized by the Authority. In addition to the above the QPPV and the Back-up QPPV should have knowledge on applicable Ghanaian safety monitoring legislation and guidelines and international standards for Pharmacovigilance and also demonstrate (e.g. through qualifications and training) that he/she has knowledge of the key pharmacovigilance activities performed as part of the MAH’s pharmacovigilance system and how to implement them.

candidates.statement: 3.3.4 Responsibilities of QPPV The QPPV shall not be freelance, but an employee of the MAH or the Local Representative of the MAH. The responsibilities of the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance shall include but not limited to the following:
candidates.context: v. Participation in at least one pharmacovigilance conference OR training programme relevant to patient safety OR passing a written exam related to the QPPV roles administered by the Food and Drugs Authority. i. Act as a single point of contact for the Authority on all matters relating to pharmacovigilance and safety of marketed products including pharmacovigilance inspections.

candidates.statement: All RMPs submitted shall be accompanied by a declaration to be signed by the QPPV (Refer Appendix III). The declaration should indicate that the QPPV has read the RMP and will ensure implementation of all activities outline in the RMP.
candidates.context: iv. Prepare the following documents for submission to the Authority; a. Adverse Drug Reaction reports b. Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs)/Periodic Benefit- Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRER), when necessary c. Company-sponsored pre- and post-registration study reports d. Risk Management Plans and Ghana Specific Risk Management Plan when requested by the Authority. e. Ongoing pharmacovigilance evaluation during the post- registration period.

candidates.statement: In view of responsibilities listed above, the QPPV role shall be a full-time job. The FDA therefore reserves the right to withdraw the license of any QPPV who is found to take up full- time role with another company.
